q: What is the kinetic energy of a $1500\,\text{kg}$ car when its speed is $72\,\text{km/h}$?
A $2.0\,\text{kg}$ trolley moves at $3.0\,\text{m/s}$ and sticks to a $1.0\,\text{kg}$ trolley at rest. What is the common speed of the trolleys?
a: Momentum is conserved: $2.0\,\text{kg} \cdot 3.0\,\tfrac{\text{m}}{\text{s}} = (2.0\,\text{kg} + 1.0\,\text{kg})\,v'$, so $v' = \dfrac{6.0\,\text{kg} \cdot \text{m/s}}{3.0\,\text{kg}} = 2.0\,\text{m/s}$. The kinetic energy decreases from $9.0\,\text{J}$ to $6.0\,\text{J}$.
